subject: Does the dispersal estimate matter in Negative Binomial model (gdistsamp) for 1 visit data

messages.author: a1ce4812eae6de0d
messages.subject: Does the dispersal estimate matter in Negative Binomial model (gdistsamp) for 1 visit data
parts:
Dear all,

I have run the HDS models with distsamp and gdistsamp functions with my bird point count data that I only visit the point once  (n=1348 points; birds were detected from 571 points). I first tried with the Poisson model and checked the c-hat from the global model, the c-hat value=2.94. I run the model again with a Negative Binomial and the c-hat from NB model improved (c-hat=1.27). I then choose the NB to develop the model in the further step. 

However, some of the models could not run because I need to provide start values. I have tried many combinations but it did not work. I also tried different model methods and found out that the "SANN" method could help me with this (I can eventually successfully run the model). But I got another problem, the results from different methods and different start values are different, especially the estimated value for the dispersal part and AIC value. AIC rank changed if I changed the method for the whole model set.
I attached some results from the models that I developed from the same set of covariates and data, just changing the method and start values.

My question is does the dispersal estimate matter in this case? And any recommendation to deal with the methods and start values selections? Based on my example results which one should I select?

Thank you so much in advance

Best regards,
Faii
